title: Onboarding Security Handoff for Customer‑Facing Hires
author: Priya Kapoor
summary: A focused playbook that defines a repeatable security and data‑readiness handoff for new hires whose role requires early access to customer data, accounts, or PII. Includes timeline, owner matrix, access checklists, training requirements, and audit evidence templates.
body:
Purpose:
This document defines the required steps and owner responsibilities for onboarding customer‑facing hires (Support, CSM, Solutions, Sales Eng, Account Teams, and early-product pilots) who require access to production customer data, accounts, or other restricted resources during their first 30 days. The goal is to reduce risk while enabling a fast time to impact through a clear, auditable security handoff.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to any role that requires read or write access to customer PII, production databases, live logs, or customer tenant environments within the first 30 days.
- Exclusions: strictly marketing-only hires, contractors with strictly non‑prod access (see contractor onboarding policy).

Why this exists:
- Customer‑facing roles often need access early to do demos, troubleshooting, or account work. Uncoordinated access creates security, compliance, and support risk.
- This playbook balances speed and control with automated checks and human approvals so hires are productive without bypassing controls.

Core SLOs (service level objectives):
- Access readiness: 90% of approved hires have required low‑risk access by Day 2 and high‑risk access by Day 10.
- Training completion: 100% completion of mandatory security and data handling modules by Day 7.
- Audit evidence: 100% of access approvals recorded in the access log and associated with a signed manager attestation before Day 10.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Hiring Manager (owner of readiness): submit access intake, provide business justification, perform manager attestation.
- People Ops (onboarding coordinator): track timeline, trigger security/IT tasks, schedule buddy/mentor.
- Security (access reviewer): validate justification, apply compensating controls, approve or deny high‑risk accesses.
- IT/Cloud Ops (provisioning): create accounts, grant groups/roles, enable MFA.
- Customer Success/Support buddy (operational trainer): run shadowing sessions and approve operational readiness.

Access categories (definitions):
1) Low risk: non‑production dashboards, read‑only product analytics, marketing CRM non‑PII fields.
2) Medium risk: internal tooling with customer identifiers (non‑PII), staging tenant access, runbook modification rights.
3) High risk: production customer PII, customer tenant admin roles, ability to modify production customer resources, billing and contract systems.

Access decision matrix (text table):
- Low risk: Manager approval + People Ops intake -> grant by IT automatically after Day 0 enrollment.
- Medium risk: Manager approval + Security review -> granted after training completion and 1:1 review with buddy.
- High risk: Manager approval + Security + Legal sign-off (if PII) -> staged access with time‑boxed session and audit logging enabled; no permanent write access without 30‑day probation signoff.

Step‑by‑step process (preparing before Day 0):
1. Hiring Manager completes 'Security & Data Readiness' intake form in the People Ops portal with: justification, access categories requested, expected date of first use, proposed compensating controls if any.
2. People Ops opens ticket with Security and IT automatically.
3. Security performs risk classification and returns a checklist with mandatory training modules and any suggested mitigations (e.g., VPN only, session recording).
4. IT schedules account creation window timed for Day 0 or Day 1 depending on complexity.

Day 0 to Day 2 (initial activation):
- Day 0: account skeleton created; manager attestation email sent to Security (template below).
- Day 1: low‑risk access enabled; new hire completes MFA enrollment and baseline onboarding training (security essentials, data handling).
- Day 2: People Ops confirms training completion and triggers medium/high‑risk review if requested.

Day 3 to Day 10 (staged escalation):
- Medium risk: buddy shadowing and 1:1 operational signoff required prior to enabling write access.
- High risk: temporary elevated access window can be granted for supervised sessions (session recording and keystroke logging enabled where appropriate). Permanent wide‑scope access requires: 2 week operational shadowing + manager attestation + Security checklist complete.

Required training and certification (examples):
- Mandatory: Security Essentials for Customer Teams (1 hr), Data Handling Basics (45 mins), Phishing & Device Hygiene (30 mins).
- Conditional: PII handling and contract‑system usage (for high risk); TPRM awareness if customer access crosses partner integrations.
- Training evidence: People Ops records completion timestamps and attaches to the onboarding ticket.

Manager attestation template (email or form snippet):
"I confirm that the access requested for [New Hire name, role] is necessary for the business function outlined. I accept ownership for monitoring usage during the initial 30‑day probation and will sign off on permanent access after operational shadowing completes. — [Manager name]"

Operational readiness checklist (must be completed & attached to ticket):
- [ ] Account created and MFA enforced
- [ ] Mandatory training completed (timestamps)
- [ ] Buddy shadowing scheduled (dates)
- [ ] Manager attestation received
- [ ] Security review complete (if medium/high)
- [ ] Audit logging configured for high‑risk actions

Examples & CLI snippets (internal tooling):
- Grant group (example): rbaccmd grant --user newhire@redwood.ai --group cs-readonly --expires 2026-09-01
- Create ticket (People Ops automation): peopleops-cli create-onboard --name "New Hire" --access "customer-read" --mgr "manager@redwood.ai"
(Replace commands with the equivalent in our internal tooling; automation will normally invoke these steps.)

Audit evidence & retention:
- Every access grant must include: intake form ID, manager attestation record, training completion artifacts, security review ID, provisioning ticket ID.
- Retention: store onboarding evidence for 7 years in the compliance bucket (encrypted). Searchable index keys: hire_id, intake_id, manager.

Acceptance criteria & signoff (for permanent high‑risk access):
- Operational competency demonstrated (buddy signoff).
- No security exception raised during supervised period.
- Manager and Security both sign the access change ticket. The ticket must be closed with final signoff comments and timestamp.

Compensating controls for early access (temporary options):
- Read‑only modes, timeboxed sessions, increased logging, shadowing with recorded sessions, limiting access to specific tenants only.

Escalation & exceptions flow:
1. Manager requests exception via People Ops (include business justification, risk mitigations).
2. Security reviews and issues a conditional temporary grant (timeboxed or scoped).
3. Legal review required if PII handling or contract systems are involved.
4. Any exception longer than 30 days must be approved by Head of Security + Head of People Ops.

Metrics to track (dashboards):
- Time to first useful access (by risk category).
- Percentage of hires completing mandatory training by Day 7.
- Number of temporary exception grants and their average duration.
- Audit gaps (missing attachments) per onboarding ticket.

Related pages & templates:
- People Ops intake form (internal link): /confluence/people-ops/onboarding-intake-forms
- Security training modules: /confluence/security-and-compliance/training-catalog
- Access request automation: /confluence/eng-infra/automation/request-scripts

Appendix A: Example manager attestation (form JSON as text):
{
  "hire_name": "[Name]",
  "role": "[Role]",
  "requested_access": "[Low/Medium/High]",
  "manager": "[Manager email]",
  "attestation_timestamp": "YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ"
}
(Attach this JSON as text to the People Ops ticket; our automation will parse it.)

Appendix B: Common pitfalls and remediations:
- Pitfall: Manager over‑requests high‑risk access without a plan. Remediation: require a detailed runbook and temporary scope.
- Pitfall: Training incomplete but access created. Remediation: automation rejects medium/high grants until completion timestamps are present.

Owner and review cadence:
- Document owner: People Ops (Priya Kapoor).
- Reviewers: Security (Aisha Banerjee), IT/Cloud Ops (Marco Lopez), Customer Success (Samir Patel).
- Review cadence: annual or on significant product/ compliance changes.

Questions or exceptions: contact people-ops@redwood.ai and security@redwood.ai.
